_about.purpose: Single source of truth for every quantitative claim in this project. results/README.md is GENERATED from this file by scripts/render_results.py, so numbers cannot drift between the two.

provenance_status.transcribed: Number is recorded here from the run's stdout, which was captured in the git commit message at the listed SHA. The raw artifact (JSON/log/NEFF) is NOT in the repo — see _artifact_loss.
provenance_status.in_repo: Raw artifact is committed under results/raw/.

_about._artifact_loss: The trn2 instance used for all measurements expired on 2026-08-02. Every raw artifact lived in /tmp on that host: measure_mfu --json-out files, neuron-explorer summary-json output, NEFF/NTFF profile pairs, and detached run logs. All are gone. The numbers survive because each run's stdout was pasted into the commit message at the time, and every producing script is committed. Nothing here is unreproducible, but nothing here is currently backed by a raw file either. `make results` regenerates the whole set into results/raw/ on a fresh instance. Logged as a sticking point: results should never have lived only on an ephemeral host.
_about.hardware: trn2.3xlarge, 1 Neuron device, 4 NeuronCores, LNC2 (2 logical cores), single logical core used unless stated
_about.compiler_flags: NEURON_CC_FLAGS unset for every measurement — compiler defaults throughout. This is a known open item: no run has confirmed the results are independent of default target/LNC selection.

measurements.notes: Amortisation test: call count is fixed by model depth, so more sequence = more work per call. 2.59x more baseline work costs only 1.16x more per call, so the residual is near-fixed and the penalty nearly halves.

measurements.notes: The override is set to whatever _detect_target() returns on the host, never hardcoded, because a wrong target would compile for the wrong hardware and could be silently wrong. cos_sim identical to 6 dp across all four, so neither fix changes what gets compiled.

measurements.what: Do N NKI calls share one XLA graph and one device execution? Counted via torch-xla ExecuteTime metric.
measurements.notes: compiles=0 on every variant, 3 samples each within 0.1%. The 28 calls DID share one graph (196 nodes = 28x7) and still cost 28x, so graph batching was never the lever. execs-before-mark_step = 0 rules out nki.jit self-synchronising.

measurements.notes: torch-xla metric accumulators are NANOSECONDS; an earlier read of them as seconds produced a nine-digit millisecond figure. Cross-check against metrics_report(), which prints explicit units.

measurements.what: Device time, NKI kernel vs the torch op it replaces, identical work both ways

marginal_traffic_regression.note: traffic(N) = FIXED + N x MARGINAL, solved from the N=1 and N=28 points. Unfused floor for a [512,3072] bf16 tile is 2 tiles = 6.29 MB.

measurements.notes: CHAINED microbenchmark: 28 identical ops back to back. This maximises the compiler's fusion opportunity and is therefore NKI's worst case. Do not quote the 2.5-2.7x ratio without the in-situ figure below. NKI marginal traffic is exactly the unfused floor, so the kernels spill nothing and the gap is the forfeited fusion, not kernel quality.

measurements.what: Real Qwen3-0.6B forward: how much of the regression is device vs dispatch
measurements.notes: THIS IS THE NUMBER TO LEAD WITH. Wall times here (46.65/146.65) come from the profiled run rather than measure_mfu (42.04/141.43) because NEURON_RT_INSPECT adds a few ms; the decomposition uses one consistent pair. HBM traffic includes weights, so the 1.42x ratio dilutes the activation-only effect and is not the fusion penalty directly.

measurements.what: nkilib fused MLP vs torch (3 matmuls + silu), device time, distinct weights per block

weight_transpose_cost.note: Finding #17 (weight layout) quantified. Separate NEFF, one-time at load rather than per step.

measurements.notes: H=1024/I=3072 is Qwen3-0.6B's MLP shape and is INSIDE Finding #18's compile limit, so this kernel works for the benchmarked model. A first version of this measurement shared one weight set across all 28 blocks, letting the compiler amortise one weight load; torch showed 12.1 MB/block against an 18.9 MB weight set, which exposed it. Fixed to per-block weights (528 MB total).

measurements.what: Fused MLP single-core compile boundary vs intermediate_size
measurements.conclusion: passes iff intermediate_size <= 4096; boundary is between 4096 and 4224; not a ratio effect
measurements.error: 'floordiv' does not allow division by zero, in nkilib/core/utils/kernel_helpers.py:104 via mlp_cte_tile_info.py:236
measurements.notes: REFRAMED by Finding #26: this is a design boundary, not a bug. A floordiv by zero on a shard-count calculation is what happens with no SPMD shard grid. Originally filed as an nki-library bug to fix.

measurements.what: All five test suites, NKI execution asserted by call counters
Is torch.compile broken on this stack? (Finding #23)
measurements.root_cause: torch_neuronx replaces certain ATen ops with XLA user computations. The dispatch predicate is `if any(is_xla_tensor(it) or is_xla_device(it) ...)`, which a FakeTensor on xla:0 satisfies, so Dynamo's fake-tensor pass is routed into _xla_user_computation and rejected. No abstract impls.
measurements.workaround: torch_xla.compile() works; verified same value as eager (sum = 902.0360)
measurements.notes: Affected list includes Embedding, Softmax and CrossEntropyLoss, so this hits essentially any transformer. Unrelated to the Kernel Hub; filed because we found it.

measurements.what: Upstream transformers coverage of the interception points we target

open_items.item: No run has confirmed the results are independent of compiler flags
open_items.detail: NEURON_CC_FLAGS was unset for every measurement. Setting --target trn2 --lnc {1,2} explicitly has not been tried. This should be the first thing re-run on a fresh instance, because a config artifact would undermine the device-time comparisons specifically.

open_items.detail: 91.6% of the remaining regression. Not attempted: inside torch_xla's op-registry path, and a wrong guess could be silently incorrect rather than error.

open_items.item: Does a kernel spanning a fused region beat the compiler on that region?
open_items.detail: The fused MLP answers this for single-core (no, by ~3x). Unmeasured multi-core with an SPMD grid, which is the configuration the kernel was built for.
